stages.name: linear disconnected-track interpolation

implementation.call_site: __main__ block, dti(txt_path, save_path, n_min=5, n_dti=20); note the signature default is n_min=25, so the signature alone would misreport this run

parameter_semantics.n_min: Minimum tracklet LENGTH, not a gap. A track is interpolated only if its retained row count strictly exceeds n_min (code: if n_frame > n_min).
parameter_semantics.n_dti: Maximum interpolated gap. A gap between consecutive retained frames is filled only if 1 < (right_frame - left_frame) < n_dti, both strict; with n_dti=20 the longest filled gap spans 19 frames and inserts 18 rows.

stages.inserted_row_marking: none. Verified at byte level on this artifact: all 2072 inserted rows and all 48169 surviving rows carry confidence -1, so the submitted file contains no field that distinguishes an inserted row from a tracked one.

split.definition: For each of the seven MOT17 TRAIN sequences of native length n, retain native frames [floor(n/2)+2 .. n] and rebase them by floor(n/2)+1 so the clip starts at frame 1; val_half length = n - floor(n/2) - 1. This is a locally derived split of the public training set, not an official benchmark split.

configuration.invocation: python scripts/run_mot_challenge.py --BENCHMARK MOT17 --SPLIT_TO_EVAL val_half --METRICS HOTA CLEAR Identity --DO_PREPROC True --USE_PARALLEL False --NUM_PARALLEL_CORES 1

resolved_settings.scoreable_reference_rule: DO_PREPROC=true keeps ground-truth rows with mark != 0 AND class == 1 (mot_challenge_2d_box.py:390-392); this rule comes from the evaluator, not from the reporter

configuration.omitted_arguments_and_why: none omitted for this benchmark. For BENCHMARK DANCE at this pinned commit, --SEQMAP_FILE and --OUTPUT_FOLDER must be omitted: run_mot_challenge.py registers every None-default argument with nargs='+', so passing either yields a one-element list and raises TypeError.

reference_side_diagnostics.scoreable_reference_definition: ground-truth rows with mark != 0 AND class == 1, i.e. the evaluator's own DO_PREPROC retention rule
